prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1199; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant, who reports being rear-ended... no wait, this is a head-on collision. Reviewing the first notice of loss: low-speed head-on collision, claimant reports neck pain and stiffness and has no lawyer representing them at this stage.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene by the claimant show the front-end damage and confirm several details of how the vehicles came together. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main visual record for now.

Entry 3: Police report obtained and it confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The responding officer's notes are consistent with the account given at first notice.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspected. The damage is mostly in line with the impact described, and the pattern of deformation fits a low-speed frontal collision. Nothing in the inspection points to earlier damage on this vehicle.

Entry 5: Checked prior claims and medical history. No earlier injury to the same body area is on record. The reported whiplash is a good match for the kind and force of this crash.

Entry 6: Coverage confirmed to be active on the date of loss, with no sign the damage predates the start of the policy. The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.

Entry 7: Spoke with the claimant again. The account has been the same in every conversation so far. Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so the medical records are being reviewed.

Entry 8: Next steps are to request the full treatment records and continue the medical review. The file remains open pending those records.
